summary: Lake Superior light at the end of the Duluth Ship Canal's north pier, first lit 7 April 1910; the 1967 pier storm killed a Coast Guardsman and three brothers.

lens.note: Original fifth-order lens by Henri Lepaute of Paris, dated 1882 (NRHP). Removed in 2014.

structures.note: NRHP: the superstructure (conical steel light tower with lantern) is 37 feet tall. The tower alone is about 28 feet (NRHP).
Rock-filled timber crib with a concrete pier (NRHP).
Frame quarters for the chief keeper of the south breakwater lights (NRHP, dated 1874); LighthouseFriends dates the head keeper's frame building to 1873.
Brick duplex built for the assistant keepers and their families (NRHP).

access.note: The deck around the light is open to public visitation; the tower interior is not. Reached on foot by the north pier. The walkway is fenced off when strong waves come over the walls.

facts.agency: Rethos (from 2023); U.S. Coast Guard before that

events.note: First light on the piers established; LighthouseFriends dates the head keeper's frame dwelling to this year. The NRHP dates the 1874 frame dwelling to the south breakwater keeper.
North pier completed; not lighted (NRHP; LighthouseFriends).
Congress appropriated $4,000 on 4 March 1909 to light the north pier (LighthouseFriends; NRHP gives the date).
Bulletin 1912 describes the light as occulting, two seconds light and two seconds eclipse, from a 5th-order fixed lens, supplied from the city electric lighting system.
Converted from oil to electric incandescent (Bulletin 1915).
Radiobeacon established at the Duluth Canal on 24 August 1927 (LighthouseFriends). A separate beacon, not the light itself.

30 April 1967: a 20-foot wave swept three brothers off the north pier; Boatswain Mate First Class Edgar A. Culbertson was swept into the canal and died. The Coast Guard Medal was awarded to the Coast Guardsmen. Accounts differ on the sequence (NWS; LighthouseFriends).
Fencing installed to close the walkway toward the light when strong waves come over the walls (NWS).
Original fifth-order Fresnel lens removed and replaced by an LED optic; range reduced from about 14 to 10.5 nautical miles (NRHP; LighthouseFriends).
National Register nomination dated 26 February 2016; listed under number 16000340.
Ownership transferred to Rethos, a St. Paul-based nonprofit (LighthouseFriends). The NRHP (2016) gives the Coast Guard as owner.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The frame dwelling is dated 1873 by LighthouseFriends and 1874 by the NRHP, which ties it to the south breakwater lights' chief keeper. Not resolved; both are shown.

The NRHP says Congress appropriated $3 million for the Duluth and Superior ports in 1895; LighthouseFriends gives an act of 3 June 1896 providing over $3 million. The story gives both and does not choose.

The 1912 Bulletin describes an occulting light (2 s light, 2 s eclipse) from a fifth-order fixed lens; the NRHP describes the current LED beacon as red, on for three seconds and off for three seconds. The record's Iso R 6s matches the current description.
The NRHP (2016) says the Coast Guard owns the light; LighthouseFriends says ownership passed to Rethos in 2023. The story gives the later owner.

LighthouseFriends gives the range after the 2014 LED change as about 10.5 nautical miles (from about 14). The NRHP says the LED 'can be seen for 16 miles in clear weather' and does not say nautical miles. The story gives both and does not reconcile them.

NWS says the Coast Guard was called to save the three brothers; LighthouseFriends says a wave swept one brother away and the crew went out to look for two boys reportedly stranded at the pierhead light. Both accounts agree on the deaths of the three brothers and of Culbertson.

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends reports that ownership was transferred to Rethos, a St. Paul nonprofit, in 2023. The NRHP nomination (2016) gives the Coast Guard as owner. Human review: the record may lag the transfer.

notes_for_editor: The USLHS roster (100 lines, 1873-1970) is filed under the Duluth Harbor North Breakwater place record, 1.6 km from this light by the record's position (USLHS positions are only to the minute). The story does not say the 1873-1909 lines were the same keepers at this light: LighthouseFriends says the pier-light keepers tended the south range lights along with the north pierhead light, and the NRHP says the same keepers maintained the North Pier Light. Editor: check whether the roster should be split at April 1910. The NRHP nomination is the main source for dates, the lens and the 1909-1910 construction; LighthouseFriends is secondary and is cited for facts only; the 1908 Board quotation reaches us through it and is not checked against the 1908 report. The 1967 accident: NWS and LighthouseFriends differ on the sequence (see resolved_conflicts); the story gives each account separately. The story names the three brothers as NWS names them. Range: the NRHP's 16 miles (LED, clear weather) and LighthouseFriends' 10.5 nautical miles are both printed in the story as the sources give them. The 1912 Bulletin's electric supply and the 1915 change to incandescent are as printed. The 1915 passage is in the Bulletin's list of changes, PDF page 30; its OCR reads 'Dulu th North Pier'. Not checked: the 1908 Lighthouse Board report, the 1909 appropriation Act, the 1910 Light List. Chronicling America was not searched for Duluth. The Rethos transfer date (2023) and the planned 2027 tours are from LighthouseFriends only; check Rethos or the Coast Guard before publishing as current. The 'harbours' spelling in the story follows the house style; the USLHS and NRHP use 'harbor'.
